---
title: Admin UI extensions
description: Add pages, dashboard widgets and user or event actions to the beamhop admin panel from a plugin, using the panel's own React.
sidebar:
  order: 11
---

import { Steps, Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A plugin can extend the admin panel with:

- **pages**, listed under Plugins in the sidebar, at `/admin/p/<plugin>/<path>`;
- **dashboard widgets**;
- **user actions**, offered on users in the panel;
- **event actions**, offered on events in the panel.

You ship a prebuilt ESM bundle, point the plugin's `ui` field at it, and the panel imports it while the plugin is
running.

## The contract

The bundle's default export is a function that receives an `AdminUiPluginApi`:

```ts
interface AdminUiPluginApi {
  pluginName: string;
  registerPage(page: { path: string; title: string; component: unknown }): void;
  registerWidget(widget: { id: string; title: string; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; component: unknown }): void;
  registerUserAction(action: { id: string; label: string; destructive?: boolean; run(pubkey: string): Promise<void> | void }): void;
  registerEventAction(action: { id: string; label: string; destructive?: boolean; run(eventId: string): Promise<void> | void }): void;
  fetch(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>;
}
```

`component` is a React component. `api.fetch(path)` calls your plugin's [admin routes](/relay/build/plugin-routes/#admin-routes)
(`/admin/api/plugins/x/<name>/<path>`) with the admin's session and the CSRF header already set. `"/stats"` and
`"stats"` are the same; absolute URLs and `..` segments are rejected, so it can't reach the rest of the admin API.
A `401` sends the admin to the sign-in page, like the panel's own requests.

## Using the panel's React

Don't bundle your own React. The panel exposes its React instance and its shadcn/ui components on
`window.__BEAMHOP_UI__` before loading plugin bundles:

```ts
interface AdminUiHost {
  React: unknown;
  ReactDOM: unknown;
  jsxRuntime: unknown;
  ui: Record<string, unknown>;   // Button, Card, Input, Badge, Table, Dialog, Switch, ...
  toast: unknown;
}
```

The simplest approach, and the one `hello` uses, is a tiny host module that reads from that global. JSX is compiled
to its `h` function, so the bundle contains no `import "react"` at all, and no bundler externals or import maps are
needed.

<Steps>

1. Add a host shim:

   ```ts title="ui/host.ts"
   const host = (globalThis as any).__BEAMHOP_UI__;
   export const h = host.React.createElement;
   export const Fragment = host.React.Fragment;
   export const { useState, useEffect, useCallback } = host.React;
   /** shadcn component if the host provides it, otherwise a plain element */
   export const ui = (name: string, fallback: string): any => host.ui?.[name] ?? fallback;
   ```

2. Compile JSX to `h`:

   ```json title="ui/tsconfig.json"
   {
     "compilerOptions": {
       "jsx": "react",
       "jsxFactory": "h",
       "jsxFragmentFactory": "Fragment"
     }
   }
   ```

3. Write the entry and register your extensions:

   ```tsx title="ui/index.tsx"
   import type { AdminUiPluginApi } from "@beamhop/sdk";
   import { h, useState, useEffect, ui } from "./host";

   const Card = ui("Card", "section");
   const Badge = ui("Badge", "span");

   export default function register(api: AdminUiPluginApi) {
     function StatsPage() {
       const [stats, setStats] = useState(null);
       useEffect(() => {
         api.fetch("/stats").then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : null)).then(setStats);
       }, []);
       return (
         <Card style={{ padding: "1rem" }}>
           <Badge>rejected: {stats?.rejected ?? "…"}</Badge>
         </Card>
       );
     }

     api.registerPage({ path: "/stats", title: "My plugin", component: StatsPage });
   }
   ```

4. Build it as a browser ESM bundle:

   ```sh
   bun build ./ui/index.tsx --outfile ./dist/ui.js --format esm --target browser --minify
   ```

   In the beamhop repo, `bun run build:plugins` builds every first-party plugin's UI.

5. Point the plugin at the bundle. The path is relative to the plugin package root:

   ```ts
   const plugin: BeamhopPlugin = {
     name: "my-plugin",
     version: "1.0.0",
     ui: "./dist/ui.js",
     setup(ctx) { /* … */ },
   };
   ```

</Steps>

<Aside type="tip" title="Prefer real imports?">
The panel also provides an import map for `react`, `react-dom`, `react/jsx-runtime` and `@beamhop/ui`. If you'd
rather write normal imports, mark those modules as `--external` when you build. The shim approach works either way.
</Aside>

## What `hello` registers

```tsx
api.registerPage({ path: "/hello", title: "Hello", component: HelloPage });
api.registerWidget({ id: "hello-rejected", title: "Hello plugin", size: "sm", component: HelloWidget });
api.registerUserAction({
  id: "hello-greet",
  label: "Say hello (example)",
  run: (pubkey) => toast(`Hello ${pubkey.slice(0, 8)}…!`),
});
```

The page polls `api.fetch("/stats")` every 5 seconds and has a button that `POST`s to `/reset`. Mark actions that
change or remove data with `destructive: true`.

## How bundles are served

- The server serves the bundle at `/admin/plugins-ui/<name>.js` (with `?v=<version>` in the URL the panel uses),
  only while the plugin is running.
- The panel imports bundles for running plugins and unloads them when a plugin is disabled.
- Widgets and actions are hidden from admins without the `plugins.use` permission (viewers), since the admin routes
  behind them would refuse those admins anyway.
- An error while loading one plugin's UI is isolated to that plugin.

<Aside type="caution">
A plugin's UI bundle runs in the admin panel's origin with the signed-in admin's session. It is as trusted as the
plugin's server code.
</Aside>
